How units behave

  • Units spawn on the roads away from the wanted character and hunt along the real road lines (Street Control → Units drive; turn it off to move them yourself).
  • Traffic pulls over for blue lights. A patrol car with no one wanted just cruises; if anyone becomes wanted it joins the hunt.
  • A unit within reach of a wanted character on foot posts a Stop! Police! card: Leg it, Talk, Come quietly, or (GM) They fight — two officers get out and the Combat Console opens.
  • At three stars India 99 sees anyone outdoors; at five, every map exit has a roadblock (Wheels, Hard, to run it).

Officers in a fight

Press Police AI on an officer's die. They go for the most wanted character: cuff anyone surrendered, Down or Grabbed; shout at one star; grab at close quarters; taser at two stars or when you are armed; CS spray and baton up close; at four stars, armed officers shoot.

GM'S BOOK

Running Combat

The Combat Console, from your side.

  1. Start a fight: select (and/or target) the tokens, Combat Console → Start a fight. From a police stop, use They fight.
  2. Begin round: everyone gets their speed dice. Press Roll for NPCs; wait for the players (the console lists who you are waiting on), or force the reveal.
  3. Reveal: the order posts to chat; the first die is up. Whoever's die it is gets the action buttons; you can act for anyone.
  4. Done — next moves the queue. At the end, bleeding and burning bite; then Begin round again.
Settings

Combat: apply damage automatically (off by default): the target's owner or the GM chooses Take hit or Dodge on the hit card, then you pick at most one condition; turn it on and hits land at once. Combat: witnessed crimes add Heat (on).

Without the Combat Console, the core combat tracker still works: initiative is d6 (exploding) + Moves, and Bleeding, Stunned, reactions and the Down countdown run at each turn.

The core Combat Tracker still works and shows each combatant's top die; its Combat Console button opens the speed-dice view.

By our Hackney reporter

Cyclists in Hackney have described bike theft in the borough as "out of control" after a spate of thefts outside cafés on Broadway Market and London Fields.

Stretch sends a text: a race across Hackney Marshes at dusk. Winner takes the patch west of the Lea. Loser gives up their bike.

Objectives

  1. Get to Hackney Marshes (ticks itself)
  2. Win the race (three Wheels rolls against Stretch)
  3. Keep your bike

£250 each3 XP+1 Chainring, +1 Street

How it plays

Three legs: the football pitches, the canal bridge, the Lea towpath. Each is an Opposed Wheels roll against Stretch (GM Screen → Checks → Opposed). Off-road bikes (Trailblazer, Dirt Devil) get +1 on the pitches.

A Proper Mess on the towpath: Come Off the Bike hazard — and the canal is right there (In the Canal).

Complication

Stretch cheats: a Lea Boy with a bike chain waits at the bridge.

Next: Win and Stretch loses face; lose and Pat loses a patch. Either way: Mission 12.

MISSION 11 · AUNTIE PAT

Raid

The Arches, Morning Lane

Five in the morning. Kez rings, breathless: three vans on Morning Lane, a dog unit, and DS Vale with a warrant. Pat is still inside with the ledger.

Objectives

  1. Get to The Arches (ticks itself)
  2. Get Pat out the back
  3. Save the ledger (teamwork: Search the Place)
  4. Lose all the Heat

£0 each5 XP+2 Chainring

How it plays

Set Heat 3 for anyone seen near the yard. Police → Police Dog and Hazards → CS Spray for the officers on the shutter. Officers get out of the vans and take their own turns in the Combat Console (Police AI). Surrendering is an option: Busted, but the ledger might be safe if someone else has it.

If Mission 8 went badly, Vale knows about the back door.

Complication

The ledger names the grass. It is someone the players like.

Next: Pat wants it finished: Mission 12.

MISSION 12 · AUNTIE PAT

Big Night

The Lea Boys' lock-up, Leyton

Pat has found where Stretch keeps his stock: a lock-up behind the Leyton Orient ground. Two hundred bikes, a van of parts, and Stretch's cash box. Tonight it ends.

Objectives

  1. Get to Leyton (ticks itself)
  2. Get into the lock-up
  3. Take Stretch's stock — or Stretch
  4. Get everyone home
  5. Face Pat's reckoning with the grass

£1000 each5 XP+2 Chainring, +1 StreetRep 3+

How it plays

The finale. Getting in: Pick a Lock, Break Down a Door, or a ram through the shutter. Inside: Stretch, four Lea Boys and a guard dog. Use the Combat Console; police arrive at Heat 3 after three rounds of gunfire, Trojans at four.

Getting the stock home is a convoy: the Tranzit van (6 seats), bikes on the back. Bow Breakers will take the van; Pat takes the bikes.

Then Pat, the ledger and the grass. Let the players decide. This is the end of "On Your Bike" — and the start of whatever they want The Smoke to be.

Complication

DS Vale has been watching the lock-up too. She lets them go — this time.

Next: Rep 3 and up: Pat's car jobs, Uncle's back room, and London beyond Hackney.

THE SMOKE · GM

The Sandbox Campaign

Twelve factions, ninety-six commissions, twenty local cases and 160 venues, every one mapped.

The opening, On Your Bike, is where the crew starts. This book turns the rest of Hackney and its neighbours into an open city: twelve organisations with eight commissions each, twenty independent cases in twenty districts, and one shared pressure — the Quiet Ledger — that sits under some of the crimes without explaining all of them.

How to use it

Every commission and case is on the Mission Board (GM Screen → Tools, or the Blower's Missions app): pick a career or Local cases at the top of the list. Renown with each faction opens its next commission and is awarded automatically when you pass a mission; Factions & Renown on the board keeps Renown, Influence and stance. Each mission page names its rooms. Every venue has its own map (MAPPED): the board's Prepare this mission's maps imports them, and walking through a venue's ENTER pin on the street map does too.

SANDBOX CAMPAIGN

The Expanded Sandbox

The starting world

Keep the current twenty street maps, four interior maps and London overview. The four interiors are the starting rooms of the campaign. Add eight interior maps to each street district: six play areas based on real places and two explicitly fictional premises. The result is 160 proposed interior maps containing 960 room zones, alongside the 25 existing room zones. Two interiors can occupy one real complex: the New Spitalfields produce hall and administration, for example, are separate play areas rather than two distinct venues.

What the crew does

The crew steals bicycles and sound systems, retrieves disputed property, carries illicit consignments, protects or betrays witnesses, works the fictional Halo drug market, follows missing people and recordings, and competes for money and control. Each of twelve organisations has eight substantial commissions. Twenty independent district cases offer thefts, sporting contests, debt disputes, an independent murder and other mysteries. The central case provides a shared pressure without being the explanation for every crime.

How the map expansion works

An offered job names the rooms the GM will need. Accepting the job brings its venue maps into play and grants a concrete approach: a guest list, event booking, dispatch introduction, visitor meeting or explicitly risky unsponsored entry. Completion can earn a repeat arrangement. Later work opens private rooms, control of a fictional business or a partnership with a named person. Public bars, foyers, worship and ordinary services remain available from the beginning; the unlock records prepared story space and earned relationships.

The map labels

MAPPED means a matching map already exists in the assessed source bundle. MAPPED means a proposed map or new venue pin has no matching playable map yet. A mapped street landmark does not supply its interior. The district cards label all 160 new interiors MAPPED; separate approach insets are also MAPPED. Room codes such as @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.d54307367c0dc599]{DA7.2} belong to their parent interior map, not six separate map commissions.

Real places and fictional play

Real names and addresses locate the campaign in London. All proposed room layouts are invented play spaces, not surveyed building plans. All named campaign contacts, criminal acts, private events, tenants and organisations are fictional. A visiting criminal at a real venue does not make its operator a faction member. The venue sources establish names and location, not campaign incidents or proposed room arrangements.

Planning status

This book is a campaign and map-production plan. The proposed maps, new location pins, access records, missions and faction rules have not been added to the game system. The source archive remains the assessed version 0.1.3. Use the register to commission maps before their scenes are run.

A crew reputation in each faction

Track Renown separately for all twelve factions, starting at 0. The rank thresholds are 0 Unproven, 3 Known, 7 Trusted, 12 Connected, 18 Insider and 25 Pillar. Rank opens the faction benefits in its profile and increases the Influence cap from 1 through 6. Public notoriety and police attention are separate fictional consequences; high Renown with a lender does not automatically impress a detective.

Eight jobs and the complete career

The eight career jobs award 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 5 and 5 Renown, for 25 across a full career. Their offer gates are 0, 1, 3, 5, 8, 11, 15 and 20. A completed previous commission normally supplies the next introduction; an equivalent local favour or another sponsor can meet the gate. The crew can work several careers, abandon a patron or earn independent contacts without completing all 96 missions.

Who earns an award

Agree the client, brief, fee and meaning of success before a job begins. Award the listed Renown once when the client accepts the completed outcome or the faction recognises the crew as its new legitimate negotiating party. A different faction may reward a disclosed new commission, but a secret double promise creates a debt and does not automatically duplicate rewards. Partial success earns 1 less Renown to a minimum of 0 and leaves a concrete recovery opportunity. Renown survives a hostile sponsor; current stance controls the services they will actually offer.

Fees and Influence

Suggested total crew fees are GBP 80, 120, 160, 240, 320, 480, 640 and 1000 by stage, plus explicitly agreed salvage. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2d9fbb694ed5e2d2.JournalEntryPage.0fb97a2328543408]{CH1} uses the existing fencing proceeds and GBP 40 order bonus instead of a second flat fee. Each accepted main job restores 1 Influence with its paying faction; a capstone restores 2, up to the current rank cap. Influence is spent for a named favour: 1 for a willing introduction, 2 for a room booking, equipment hire or paid transport arrangement, 4 for a major commitment within the faction's actual resources. Spending Influence does not erase Renown.

The first door

Every venue entry names its earliest career invitation and any local-case shortcut. The printed gate is an opportunity, not a magical lock. Accepting that commission opens its listed rooms for that visit, with the inviting NPC arranging the fictional event or meeting. The GM prepares the map before play. An independent lead can bring a map forward immediately: agree a booking price, a relationship or a risky fictional approach and its consequences. Completing a mission inside a location is never a prerequisite for that first visit.

The second door

After a recognised job, the contact offers the repeat service printed on the location card. R7 with that sponsor can make a regular appointment available; R12 can reserve an agreed work room; R18 can give a voice in the fictional project using it. These are requests and bookings with costs, not command over a real venue. At R25, only an explicitly fictional premise can offer a negotiated lease, share or cooperative seat. Resolve existing occupants, debts and weekly obligations before recording a claimed asset.

Four access states

Record Known, Entered, Trusted and Claimed for each interior. Known means an actionable lead. Entered means a playable visit has occurred. Trusted means a named repeat arrangement has been earned. Claimed applies only to fictional premises with a signed or otherwise agreed stake. Record the sponsor and permission alongside the state. Map status is separate: a Trusted location can still say MAPPED while this remains a planning document.

Local jobs and repeat work

Each independent case can award 1 Renown once to one of its named factions, plus its fee or an agreed favour. Repeat routine jobs can earn at most 6 Renown per faction per season. Repeat work pays and creates obligations, but capstones require a consequential commission or equivalent outcome. This keeps interior progression open without requiring endless identical errands.

Stance and consequences

Record each relevant patron as Open, Allied, Strained or Hostile. Change stance only when that patron knows a specific act and has a reason to react. A failed delivery produces a recovery demand; a witnessed double sale produces a claimant; an exposed betrayal can produce a faction split. Restoration needs concrete restitution, a revised agreement or a new sponsor. No single boss can erase every relationship in an organisation.

SANDBOX CAMPAIGN

Running the Open City

A session rhythm

Begin with two or three live offers, one independent lead and a visible consequence from earlier work. Let the crew choose a client and preparation. Run the named interior scenes, a pressure event and a decisive handover. At the end, record money, Renown, Influence, stance, interior access, one relationship and what each informed rival does next. The GM should always know who wants the current object, person or signature and where it will go if the crew does nothing.

Preparation and travel

Each mission lists an atlas route joining its district stops through existing map links. This is navigation through the supplied game atlas, not real driving directions. Arrival uses the proposed venue pin or a MAPPED approach inset. Do not turn a cross-tile journey into a time penalty unless a deadline was announced. A failed pursuit changes the next rendezvous to a reachable named site instead of making the mission vanish.

Using the rooms

The venue cards supply six keyed zones and a fictional connection pattern. Put a useful person, object or choice in at least three zones used by the active mission. Rooms 1 and 2 usually give public arrival and the visible scene; rooms 3 and 4 hold work or meetings; room 5 holds the contested object or record; room 6 gives a second arrival, loading point or exit. The individual scene text takes precedence where a venue type uses a different arrangement.

Pressure in play

Every career mission has an opposition paragraph with a concrete next move. Announce the approach of a collector, closing booking, departing van or scheduled performance before it happens. A miss can cost money, time, position, an object or a relationship. Essential facts remain available through a witness, duplicate or changed rendezvous. Use the system existing checks and consequences; these outlines do not create a second resolution engine.

One fictional drug market

Halo is a fictional illegal club drug and a profitable criminal commodity. The Lea Boys and Velvet Circuit dispute supply, price, debts and the harmful substitution. Missions can involve theft, recovery, sale, disposal, rescue, betrayal and power. Handle production and distribution as abstract scene objectives rather than real manufacturing or concealment instructions. The harm front changes named adults and faction decisions, rather than serving as a universal punishment for choosing criminal work.

Pirate radio and live streams

The car radio and out-of-car phone can continue to tune the selected real live streams. Scripted Dead Air programmes, dedications, station calls and evidence playback are separate fictional campaign content: use a GM handout, recorded fictional insert or explicit scene. A live internet stream cannot reliably supply a timed plot clue. Each radio commission names a studio, rehearsal room, archive or event space where the crew can act.

A living contact network

Put the contact from each new venue in the recurring cast after first use. They can buy a later service, ask repayment, introduce another district or refuse a changed bargain. They do not know everything in a faction. Keep Nia present as a person with choices; keep Pat able to prefer a small workshop; allow residents and traders to disagree about a sale. The crew can choose profitable crime, collective power, corporate work or a private exit, and each should produce playable consequences.

City turns

After about three substantial commissions, or when a visible deadline is reached, take one city turn. Choose one front whose named actor has money, people and opportunity to act. Advance it one step and show the move through a call, changed booking, visitor or physical notice. Successful intervention can hold or reverse one relevant step. Do not advance all fronts automatically or punish the crew for exploring a local case.

After the central case

Keep unplayed faction commissions available with an updated brief. A missing-person enquiry can become a witness privacy dispute; a pre-sale meeting becomes a restitution or ownership meeting; an auction becomes a recovery of sold goods. The culprit stays the same unless play actually changes responsibility. Unrelated thefts, sporting cases and resale disputes continue independently.

Five fronts with six steps each

Start each front at 0. Advance one step only when its named actors have the opportunity. The six developments are a menu of concrete moves; revise them when the crew changes the position.

Meridian acquisitions

Celia and Lark. 1: A new paid option reaches HB8. 2: A false vacancy account is circulated. 3: A pressured signature is sought at CL8. 4: Goods are booked for removal from DB8. 5: Final agreements are prepared at ST7. 6: The unchanged property transfers proceed.

Interventions Hold a specific option, preserve a tenant copy, fund an alternative or negotiate actual consent.

Lea Boys succession

Stretch Moth and Daz. 1: Daz claims another disputed recovery. 2: Moth asks for a separate meeting. 3: Stretch accepts a private investor promise. 4: Collectors demand a visible loyalty choice. 5: Two groups claim @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.11347b4b484f139e]{CL7} books and room. 6: A chosen group takes control unless opposed.

Interventions Settle a particular claim, back a funded successor or agree a limited division of income.

Halo harm and debt

Owen and fictional suppliers. 1: A changed load reaches LY8. 2: A buyer disputes its contents. 3: A named adult needs help after a fictional incident. 4: Suppliers demand payment for the disputed load. 5: An independent handler offers testimony or a sale. 6: The remaining load is sold removed or seized according to play.

Interventions Recover the named load, fund help, preserve an account, buy it or contest the debt.

Station independence

Patch Dee and their creditors. 1: An equipment hire bill falls due. 2: A sponsor asks for a guaranteed slot. 3: A performer refuses the proposed programme. 4: A recording buyer makes an exclusive offer. 5: The mobile programme needs money and crew. 6: A funded patron or the independent collective sets the schedule.

Interventions Pay a bill, book a viable event, recover equipment or accept a disclosed sponsor with defined terms.

Witness pressure

Rusk and any informed rival. 1: A collector asks for a witness appointment. 2: An intermediary receives an attractive offer. 3: A copy changes hands without its context. 4: A witness changes their intended meeting. 5: The final-night transport is challenged. 6: The account reaches the chosen recipient or remains private.

Interventions Agree a willing meeting, protect a particular copy, pay a real journey or expose the specific threat.

The Quiet Ledger (GM Truth)

What really happened. Keep it from the players — let them find it.

The six properties

Meridian Renewal targets six fictional occupied premises: @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.a720d397aea87d6a]{HB8} Orchard Lease Office, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.11347b4b484f139e]{CL8} Clapton Union Rooms, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5b42c691f95a7c91]{DB8} Essex Dry Goods, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.383dbdd7a30c9ab9]{VW8} White Post Workers Rooms, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.0e780ec36ad51135]{OF8} Roman Rooms Printworks and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF8} Carpenters Breakfast Club. Celia Voss approved acquisition work based on false vacancy accounts and coercive pressure. Some residents would consider a fair move; the false mandate removes their ability to negotiate one.

The payments

Evan Lark uses fictional Quayline Advisory, based in @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.cbb65680f5cc95c5]{CG8} Quayline Records Suite, to connect options, consultancy fees and apparently separate event contracts. No one folder proves everything. A dated early offer, a tenant copy and a corresponding payment support the property claim. The crew can expose it, bargain over it, buy into it or sell a supported account to an informed client.

The intimidation

Martin Rusk of @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.9f4c6205e899377d]{WW8} East Cross Security Compound escalated intimidation and a false official story to make the six sites look untenable. Owen Pike authorised a harmful Halo substitution after Rusk paid for disruption. Holt accepted consultancy money and helped the official account. Dunn retained an original record. Vale investigates specific supported offences and cannot guarantee immunity or command the whole police organisation.

The false programme

Rusk paid freelance producer Bram Senn through Owen for a misleading programme assembled from old genuine Nia audio. Seth Calder retained an earlier mix at @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.383dbdd7a30c9ab9]{VW7} Wallis Tape Rooms. Cleaner Gemma Hale has an independent copy. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.69084b39c04899a0]{HM8} Silt Listening Bunker contains an earlier rehearsal; Leon at @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5a3e0570dd504786]{LF8} can identify the old station ident. The message is fabricated even though parts of the voice are genuine.

Nia is alive

Nia Switch Bell is alive at @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.9f4c6205e899377d]{WW7} Willow Cabin with Asha Stone at the start. She compared an early tenant offer with accounts heard through her programme, then recognised her old voice in the fabricated warning. She chose to leave her conspicuous routine. Finding her, obtaining her account, preserving her originals and naming her whereabouts are four different decisions. Asha will facilitate a willing meeting when a credible intermediary agrees to Nia terms.

The Quiet Hour

The planned final event coordinates a public programme, property signatures, removal traffic and a carefully timed official narrative. These have separate control points and responsible people. The crew does not need to max every faction or solve every case before acting. Three supported strands can prompt a credible intervention; a narrower fact can still win a limited bargain. A complete public account needs the limits and provenance of its evidence stated.

Changing the truth through play

These are starting responsibilities, not a predetermined ending. Captured payments can be redirected, a buyer can withdraw, a witness can refuse publication and a faction can replace its leader. Record what the crew actually proves and what remains inference. A criminal crew may knowingly preserve part of the scheme for profit; show who gains and who is left with a claim.

Three routes to every central truth

Give the essential lead when the crew reaches the relevant source. Checks decide speed, cost, position or extra leverage. Independent routes make the mystery playable even when the crew refuses a faction or loses an original.

E1 The six premises were selected before the public trouble

Independent routes @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.d0f2613ac1d23e6b.JournalEntryPage.686cfe0a6ca772f2]{RT5} at @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.a720d397aea87d6a]{HB8} and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.11347b4b484f139e]{CL8}: independent tenant and clerk copies. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.6f05d96dac3745b1.JournalEntryPage.5b2b7a5f03feae52]{GE3} or @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.6f05d96dac3745b1.JournalEntryPage.bddb5d733296d877]{GE6}: a sale inventory and earlier offer at @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.cbb65680f5cc95c5]{CG2} or CG7. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.380caf621239c12b.JournalEntryPage.dbfa4bc0c98be132]{BM3} or @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.1181185673dbd03b.JournalEntryPage.b6a16f3432ae9a6d]{MR4} at @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.0e780ec36ad51135]{OF8} and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.25c01e80cc3ba50e]{WS7}: a print proof predating the reported emergency.

What this establishes Proves the earlier selection and false vacancy account; it does not alone prove the Halo substitution.

E2 The Halo load was deliberately changed

Independent routes @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.985bf9584d9294e7.JournalEntryPage.cc7f487551ebb84f]{LB3} or @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.985bf9584d9294e7.JournalEntryPage.f4d5d00a1615da84]{LB4} at @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b096f49f5fcfe272]{LY8}: surviving cargo and a willing handler. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2fcc7b0410f4f526.JournalEntryPage.4317f82b3e99cd92]{VC4} at @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.383dbdd7a30c9ab9]{VW5}: Owen fictional promoter account and payment dispute. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.380caf621239c12b.JournalEntryPage.20b3857b08eff2d6]{BM4} or @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.5816796be7174f14.JournalEntryPage.179900d7fa46d217]{LD5} at @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.ce26d88c705b4b63]{AE3} and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.78f07d621cc24fad]{BG8}: consenting adults and separate records.

What this establishes Supports a deliberate harmful substitution; preserve the distinction between medical treatment and a witness voluntary account.

E3 The apparent live warning was assembled from older audio

Independent routes @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.7052e00fca53338b.JournalEntryPage.9be7898e52301b3b]{AD2} at @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5a3e0570dd504786]{LF8}: old station ident and a genuine earlier contribution. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.d0f2613ac1d23e6b.JournalEntryPage.25ee7f45599e1ca8]{RT4} or @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.7052e00fca53338b.JournalEntryPage.009348f7647607d7]{AD5} at @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.383dbdd7a30c9ab9]{VW7} and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.69084b39c04899a0]{HM8}: earlier mix and rehearsal. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e88d889809aabec7.JournalEntryPage.5086e6b32e6611c5]{NM2} at @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.d54307367c0dc599]{DA4}, or @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e88d889809aabec7.JournalEntryPage.712e9b663aeacd7d]{NM7} at @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.d54307367c0dc599]{DA1}: a separately circulated recording.

What this establishes Demonstrates the programme is fabricated. Identifying every commissioner needs the financial and witness strands too.

E4 Nia is alive and chose to leave her routine

Independent routes @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.d0f2613ac1d23e6b.JournalEntryPage.0d1854ec0da2448e]{RT1} at @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5b42c691f95a7c91]{DB7}: Asha agreed contact path and a recent message. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.992bca85973f5687.JournalEntryPage.1b91cd2cc2d33577]{TU5} at @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.9f4c6205e899377d]{WW6}: a voluntary recent sighting with a safe intermediary. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.7052e00fca53338b.JournalEntryPage.2ab4a71b7ea098aa]{AD7} or @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.d0f2613ac1d23e6b.JournalEntryPage.f371e3df5645797b]{RT6} at @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.9f4c6205e899377d]{WW7}: a willing meeting with Nia.

What this establishes Finding Nia does not itself entitle the crew to broadcast her account or publish her current address.

E5 Private payments and the official story overlap

Independent routes @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.992bca85973f5687.JournalEntryPage.ab969db53150ff8e]{TU3} or @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.1181185673dbd03b.JournalEntryPage.8b155178b6ba57c7]{MR3}: driver evidence from @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.69084b39c04899a0]{HM4} and WW8. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.5816796be7174f14.JournalEntryPage.7b640abfbcb175ce]{LD2} or @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.5816796be7174f14.JournalEntryPage.6d63a16302606476]{LD6}: retained original, contractor comparison and Holt consultancy. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.b6f2c39b51dec5f2.JournalEntryPage.0001dbbd03496b6f]{BB3} or @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.6f05d96dac3745b1.JournalEntryPage.f438e557eae74cba]{GE5}: promoter payments and a separate Lark-linked account.

What this establishes Supports specific payments and false statements when dates and sources are compared; no single receipt proves the whole conspiracy.

E6 The Quiet Hour is coordinated across four fronts

Independent routes @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.992bca85973f5687.JournalEntryPage.5f6a9fc17d4ae6dc]{TU7} or @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.5816796be7174f14.JournalEntryPage.1fb049db18a7ccb6]{LD7} at @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF7}: timed dispatches and the actual customer. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.1181185673dbd03b.JournalEntryPage.1c6a4266500f4558]{MR7} at @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.7f001857f6166eed]{ST7} and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.9f4c6205e899377d]{WW8}: signature timing and contractor brief. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.7052e00fca53338b.JournalEntryPage.ff3b1ea8bdffa686]{AD8} or @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.d0f2613ac1d23e6b.JournalEntryPage.a24b58c37ba6a994]{RT7}: programme instructions and the collection offered for purchase.

What this establishes Supports coordination. The crew still chooses which fronts it can change and what account it can responsibly sell or publish.

SANDBOX CAMPAIGN

Starting Nights and Personal Stakes

The existing opening

Preserve @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2d9fbb694ed5e2d2.JournalEntryPage.0fb97a2328543408]{CH1} On Your Bike, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2d9fbb694ed5e2d2.JournalEntryPage.b24d3a40394a0516]{CH2} The Whippet and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2d9fbb694ed5e2d2.JournalEntryPage.31fe63f142ee4d21]{CH3} Lights and Sirens. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2d9fbb694ed5e2d2.JournalEntryPage.0fb97a2328543408]{CH1} begins with Mo and Pat in the mapped flat and Arches, then expands to London Fields and HC7. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2d9fbb694ed5e2d2.JournalEntryPage.b24d3a40394a0516]{CH2} restores the original Broadway Market coffee-rack setting. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2d9fbb694ed5e2d2.JournalEntryPage.31fe63f142ee4d21]{CH3} retains Morning Lane, Waterden and Bow Breakers, then opens HM7. Their new interior scenes expand the opening instead of replacing its core cast or order.

The first three sessions

Session one: run @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2d9fbb694ed5e2d2.JournalEntryPage.0fb97a2328543408]{CH1} and introduce the first storehouse. Offer @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.7052e00fca53338b.JournalEntryPage.531b033a95279cd6]{AD1} for stolen speakers and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.380caf621239c12b.JournalEntryPage.32a92965918487e6]{BM1} for a meal-and-receipt favour. Session two: follow the chosen offer or @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2d9fbb694ed5e2d2.JournalEntryPage.b24d3a40394a0516]{CH2}; show one consequence from a claimant. Session three: offer @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2d9fbb694ed5e2d2.JournalEntryPage.31fe63f142ee4d21]{CH3}, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.992bca85973f5687.JournalEntryPage.cc77fcdd90b2424a]{TU1} and the local case in the district the crew prefers. A new career can start at stage 1 whenever a named sponsor agrees to the commission.

Jaz Kaur

Jaz is 21, a Dalston rider and mechanic who wants a legitimate shop and has a bond with Kez. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC8} offers a possible garage, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b1c3f967b6aa7594]{HR8} a sporting workshop and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.db462a370713a911.JournalEntryPage.957a87da24e85625]{CH8} a defined business stake. Give Jaz a chance to pay a deposit and choose a client list, rather than declaring the shop earned by a single high roll.

Danny Tealeaf Doyle

Danny is 24 and from Homerton. He owes Pat after his mother's funeral and wants a large score. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.db462a370713a911.JournalEntryPage.541dbf4f06b2aa0b]{CH4}, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.985bf9584d9294e7.JournalEntryPage.cc7f487551ebb84f]{LB3} and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.6f05d96dac3745b1.JournalEntryPage.bddb5d733296d877]{GE6} offer increasingly profitable objects with competing claims. Pat can offer a negotiated debt reduction in place of some cash, but Danny chooses whether to accept.

Femi Adebayo

Femi is 19 and from Clapton, a former school runner who wants a trainer-brand sponsorship. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.db462a370713a911.JournalEntryPage.91c2e8f69243e771]{CH5}, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.9f3d5bcde34ec080.JournalEntryPage.43e544512ad2ec27]{S10} and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.9f3d5bcde34ec080.JournalEntryPage.29f6bfb5c06395f9]{S17} give sporting showcases and credible introductions. A genuine sponsor asks for appearances and a public reputation; a criminal patron can supply money faster while demanding a different kind of loyalty.

Big Sal Moretti

Sal is 26 and from Bethnal Green, Pat's nephew, and wants to run the crew. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.db462a370713a911.JournalEntryPage.168214c02948a6c4]{CH7}, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.985bf9584d9294e7.JournalEntryPage.cb91b5ade40c2d38]{LB7} and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.9f3d5bcde34ec080.JournalEntryPage.6990428a48394631]{S13} offer leadership, a public contest and consequences for other workers. A vote or a negotiated stake is stronger than inherited authority. Sal can build an independent faction or align with an existing patron.

pages.name: The Final Night and Later Campaigns

text.content:
SANDBOX CAMPAIGN

The Final Night and Later Campaigns

When to bring the fronts together

Start the final night when the crew has committed to a meaningful position and the responsible factions have prepared their next move. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.7052e00fca53338b.JournalEntryPage.ff3b1ea8bdffa686]{AD8}, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2fcc7b0410f4f526.JournalEntryPage.c19a5cc4367c0ae7]{VC8}, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.992bca85973f5687.JournalEntryPage.01b43c4291081cb5]{TU8}, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.380caf621239c12b.JournalEntryPage.71478f1c8a685daf]{BM8}, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.5816796be7174f14.JournalEntryPage.1fb049db18a7ccb6]{LD7}, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.1181185673dbd03b.JournalEntryPage.1c6a4266500f4558]{MR7} and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.d0f2613ac1d23e6b.JournalEntryPage.4189bb0e67e391ed]{RT8} are different commissions into the same evolving night. Run the event once. Other capstones become preparation or aftermath, with their own rewards for distinct work. Stage 8 does not require every other stage 8 to be completed first.

Three announced turns

Use Arrival, Commitment and Consequence. At Arrival, establish who is present and what each front will do next. At Commitment, signatures, cargo and the public slot begin moving. At Consequence, resolve the actions that were not changed. Give the crew one principal field operation per turn and assign named allies to other achievable tasks. State capacity, transport and permission before accepting an ally plan; a high Influence score does not create unlimited teams.

Public programme

@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.7f001857f6166eed]{ST8} Bridge Nine Broadcast Garage controls the fictional mobile programme. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC2} Round Chapel or the fictional event wing of @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.7f001857f6166eed]{ST2} can host a public gathering. AD, VC and RT can supply different accounts and performers. A supported report, an edited propaganda slot, a private bargain or a cancelled programme each changes who trusts the station. Any external transmitter site or additional stage beyond these map briefs is MAPPED.

Money and signatures

@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.7f001857f6166eed]{ST7} Meridian Sales Pavilion and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.cbb65680f5cc95c5]{CG8} Quayline Records Suite hold the current agreements; @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.a720d397aea87d6a]{HB5} can host an invented hearing. Celia and Lark can offer a stake, sign revised terms, withdraw or insist on the existing sale. The crew can bargain with complete or partial evidence. A frozen contract does not automatically repay workers or decide where occupants will live.

Premises and people

@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF8}, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.383dbdd7a30c9ab9]{VW8} and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.11347b4b484f139e]{CL8} hold the immediate property and welfare choices. BM, the occupants and any chosen ally decide which possessions, rooms and agreements they will protect. A tenant can accept a properly disclosed offer while another holds out. A crew-owned criminal base still needs a real agreement with its previous users.

Transport and the official account

@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF7} dispatches the timed loads; @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.9f4c6205e899377d]{WW8} holds Rusk contractor coordination; @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF6} gives a public passenger rendezvous. TU can redirect a willing driver, LD can preserve a specific record and CH can recover a particular vehicle. The crew must say which load or person it is moving. Routine market business remains distinct from the coercive removal and the evidence transfer.

Public exposure ending

A supported public account and surviving originals can halt particular agreements and trigger an investigation. Record which responsible people are actually implicated and which debts remain. New missions concern restitution, displaced trade, a station funding gap and rival bids for the newly available assets.

Independent coalition ending

The crew helps occupants, drivers, performers and the station negotiate a funded alternative. They gain a defined voice or stake and the work of keeping it viable. Begin the next season with a supplier failure, a difficult allocation and an attractive takeover bid.

Criminal consolidation ending

The crew uses the evidence, drug debt or transport leverage to take control of fictional premises and faction income. Track the new opposition: dispossessed patrons, unpaid workers, customers and specific investigators. Their power creates protection, recovery and succession missions instead of an automatic moral verdict.

Corporate partnership ending

The crew takes a Meridian role or negotiates a revised acquisition. Write down the price, actual signatories, protected people and excluded claims. Later play concerns an investor withdrawal, a promise the new owners cannot afford and a rival holding a surviving copy.

Private exit or fracture ending

A private sale can buy Pat's workshop, fund Jaz's garage or settle Danny's debt while leaving other fronts unresolved. If the crew splits, give each group a concrete asset and obligation. A failed intervention changes the premises, programme or patron; it does not delete the remaining sandbox.

SANDBOX CAMPAIGN

Faction Relationships

Who helps whom, and who will never forgive what.

Each relationship describes a practical conflict and a way the crew can change it. A truce can be local and partial. An uninformed faction does not react to an undiscovered betrayal.

FactionsPressureA playable change
CH and LBPat and Stretch claim the same van and frame income.CH3 and LB2 can establish a disclosed division; a secret second sale creates a specific recovery dispute.
CH and TURepairs need drivers and drivers need functioning vehicles.TU2 can turn a recovery into a paid vehicle arrangement; TU8 needs a named driver rather than a general faction promise.
CH and MRMeridian can save Pat alone while buying out neighbouring workers.CH6 and CH8 can secure a private workshop, a collective bid or a defined corporate stake.
AD and VCPerformers and equipment cross between independent radio and promoters.AD1 and VC1 can share a paid sound system; Owen cannot buy editorial consent with a booking fee alone.
AD and LBCollectors want a payment and influence over the programme.AD4 can settle a debt, back an internal split or create a rival station patron.
AD and RTThe archive has commercial value and can support a public account.AD5 and RT4 distinguish a genuine voice from a fabricated programme; the owner still chooses publication terms.
AD and MRMeridian wants a reliable slot and a respectable sponsor story.MR6 and AD8 can produce a disclosed sponsorship, independent programme or contested propaganda deal.
LB and BBLenders fund cargo and succession claims.LB5 and BB5 identify genuine accounts and invented pressure; repayment and leadership remain separate choices.
LB and BMCollectors and residents compete for the same money and rooms.LB8 and BM5 can create a limited local settlement while wider criminal income continues.
LB and MRStretch wants investor money; Moth suspects the promised future.LB6 and MR5 reveal whether the occupied fictional premises survive the deal.
VC and TUThe same vehicles carry performers, equipment and profitable contraband.VC8 and TU7 require the crew to identify each actual passenger and load.
VC and LDThe harmful Halo substitution links promoter money with a specific incident.VC4 and LD5 can preserve an account while other nightlife work continues independently.
GE and NMCollectors need resale contacts and resellers need valuations.GE1 and NM3 can establish a disclosed brokerage; a forged title produces a named buyer claim.
GE and MRRespectable art and event transactions conceal private property interests.GE5 and GE6 can expose matching dates, sell informed leverage or offer the crew a role in the transaction.
BB and MRA profitable contract can convert personal debt into property control.BB6 and MR7 can settle particular loans while leaving other accounts open.
NM and BMMarket traders and residents face the same occupied-premises sale.NM6 and BM6 can fund a genuine relocation, preserve a business or divide the coalition over price.
TU and LDDriver testimony may contradict a contractor and an official record.TU3 and LD2 reward a supported account, not a blanket promise of immunity.
BM and RTWitness support and public investigation need different permissions.BM7 and RT6 can protect Nia without making her present address part of the public story.
LD and MRHolt consultancy and Rusk false account overlap with legitimate business.LD6 and MR8 can isolate specific responsibility while a revised acquisition still proceeds.
RT and GEThe same original can be evidence, a family possession and a valuable sale.RT7 and GE8 settle custody, reproduction and sale rights separately.

SANDBOX CAMPAIGN

Map Production and Approach Insets

Which maps to make first, and the brief for the artist.

Status: every map is drawn

As of The Smoke 0.4.0, all 160 interiors (960 rooms) and all 51 approach insets below are drawn and in the London Venues compendium, and every entrance pin is on its street map. The production order is kept as the record of the plan. Only the two conditional additions (an extra boat cabin for S03, an extra stage) remain NEED MAP.

The production list contains 160 new interiors and 51 additional exterior approach insets. Every one is MAPPED. The 160 new venue entrance pins also need to be added to the existing street maps. This is a scoped production plan; none of the proposed artwork is present yet.

Prepare the accepted job first, including all the interiors and approaches it uses. The waves below group locations by their earliest faction-career appearance; independent cases and player choices can bring a later wave forward. A wave is not a universal character level or a requirement to finish the whole previous batch.

Wave 1 first appearances

36 interiors MAPPED. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.a720d397aea87d6a]{HB4}, Standard interior brief for the map artist

Use the six keyed zones from the location card. Provide a public arrival, at least two viable scene approaches, room for a conversation or confrontation, a contested object or record, and a secondary arrival or departure. The default suggested footprint is 32 by 24 squares. Sports sites use about 40 by 28, depots and market halls 44 by 28, stadium and retail event wings 48 by 32, and the boat 36 by 16. These are proposed game scales, not physical dimensions of the real buildings.

Use clearly fictional internal geometry. Each map needs a title, its site code, six room labels, entrance markers and a connection to the named atlas anchor or MAPPED inset. A large real complex is represented by the event wing or functional area used in play; it is not a claim to cover the entire building.

Source Notes and GM Records

Map inventory is grounded in the supplied source archive the-smoke-source-v0.1.3.zip, its twenty-entry street atlas, four-entry interior atlas, content and overview. The source hash at assessment was d5b94bbe72e68d1162cbaf58e0e72f16ce197ebb71c740a496bc06f4e9d5b6e1.

The real-place entries use public venue, operator, council, heritage and selected directory sources checked during this planning revision. Each real-location card links to its supporting page. Full URLs are retained in the text map register and authoring notes. A source verifies the place identity or address, not the invented campaign contact, room layout, fictional crime or proposed game price.

Some sites fall beyond a drawn side street or the edge of a tile. Their host district is a proposed campaign assignment, and their missing approach is explicitly MAPPED. The artist should resolve the frontage against the real address when drawing that inset. The current atlas is a game navigation model rather than a precise geographic survey.

Validation covered all 160 location uses, eight interiors in every district, 960 new room references, all continuation codes, existing anchor IDs and interdistrict routes. The book is an outline for preparation, with no claim of playtesting. The system source and its maps were not modified.

FACTION · CH

The Chainring

Auntie Pat. Bicycle theft and recovery, repairs, fencing and neighbourhood leverage.

Pat wants a crew that earns quietly and keeps the shop alive. She trades in stolen goods, but recognises a difference between taking a profitable risk and making a frightened neighbour pay for it. Her offer of a stake is real if the crew can carry obligations as well as money.

Bases @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.ce26d88c705b4b63]{AR4 Pat's Office [MAPPED]} / @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC7 Chainring Storehouse [MAPPED]}

People and division

Spanner Rob wants a sustainable workshop; Kez wants people treated as friends rather than expendable runners. Pat prefers discretion, Spanner wants more legitimate work, and Sal's ambition can attract members who want a more forceful operation. None automatically speaks for everyone else.

Trust and repair

Knowingly abandoning a promised recovery or selling Pat's contacts to a rival strains access. A disclosed mistake can be repaired through restitution.

Leyton Orient stadium · Lee Valley VeloPark · Kingsland Courier Arch · The Kenton · Goldsmiths Riding Workshop

CH6 · THE CHAINRING · AUNTIE PAT

The Shop That Was Already Sold

Orchard Lease Office · Essex Dry Goods · Clapton Union Rooms · Stoke Newington Town Hall

A man called Lark has offered Pat a tidy sum to walk away from the Arches, and he talks about the street as if half of it is already empty. It isn't. Pat wants to know who Lark works for before she signs anything.

Objectives

  1. Find the acquisition schedule at the Orchard Lease Office (ticks itself)
  2. Compare offers with the workers at Essex Dry Goods and the Clapton Union Rooms (ticks itself)
  3. Confront or bargain with Lark at the property meeting in Stoke Newington Town Hall
  4. Decide: protect Pat alone, build a collective bid, sell the timing evidence or take Meridian's role

£480 crew fee5 XP+4 Renown · The Chainring+1 InfluenceOffer: Renown 11

The job. Pat has been offered a private exit while other occupied premises are described as vacant. She wants the intermediary identified and her future settled.

Scenes. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.a720d397aea87d6a]{HB8.4} contains an earlier acquisition schedule. At @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.a720d397aea87d6a]{HB5.3}, an invented property meeting gives the crew a chance to confront Lark or bargain privately.

Route and checks. HB / CG / DB / CG / DA / HC / CL / SN / HB. Savvy for the date pattern; Front for terms; Bottle under financial pressure.

Pressure

Lark offers Pat money before the tenants compare their copies. The meeting closes one offer, but surviving owners and records remain available afterward.

The choice

Protect Pat alone, build a collective bid, sell the timing evidence or support Meridian for a defined role.

What follows

The agreed outcome sets Pat's award. The six-property scheme becomes a supported lead; a private bargain can preserve the shop while creating opposition when neighbours learn its terms.

CH8 · THE CHAINRING · AUNTIE PAT

Keys to the Arches

Chainring Storehouse · Clifden Crew Garage · Glasshouse Saleroom · Meridian Sales Pavilion

Pat is offering you keys. Not to the shutter: to the business. Meridian's last move lands on Morning Lane the same week, and what the Chainring becomes now depends on what you sign, and for whom.

Objectives

  1. Choose the base and its obligations: the Storehouse or the Clifden garage
  2. Find a buyer or a backer at the Glasshouse Saleroom (ticks itself)
  3. Be at the Meridian Sales Pavilion when the papers are signed (ticks itself)
  4. Recover the pledged asset before another crew collects it
  5. Decide what the business becomes, and where Pat stands in it

£1000 crew fee5 XP+5 Renown · The Chainring+2 InfluenceOffer: Renown 20

Where

@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC7 Chainring Storehouse} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC8 Clifden Crew Garage} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.cbb65680f5cc95c5]{CG7 Glasshouse Saleroom} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.7f001857f6166eed]{ST7 Meridian Sales Pavilion} MAPPED

How it plays

The job. Pat offers the crew a permanent stake while Meridian's final operation reaches the district. This decides what the business becomes.

Scenes. Choose the base and its obligations at @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC7.5} and HC8.4. A fictional sale at @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.cbb65680f5cc95c5]{CG7.2} supplies a buyer or alternative financier. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.7f001857f6166eed]{ST7.4} is the signing opportunity; another crew is collecting one pledged asset.

Route and checks. HC / DA / CG / DA / HC / WS / VW / ST. Front for ownership; Graft for the last practical job; Wheels for the competing collection.

Pressure

Rusk's collector and a tenant delegation expect incompatible promises. Resolve one immediate recovery or negotiation during each final-night turn.

The choice

The Whole City Listening

Bridge Nine Broadcast Garage · The View Tube · Round Chapel · London Stadium

The Quiet Hour has begun. Patch is handing the crew the station's defining night: one broadcast that all of east London will hear. A sponsor, a street boss and a witness all want the same slot.

Objectives

  1. Take the mobile studio at the Bridge Nine Broadcast Garage (ticks itself)
  2. Collect the last account from the courier at the View Tube (ticks itself)

  5. Decide what the city hears

FACTION · LB

The Lea Boys

Stretch or the leadership chosen in play. Street debts, intimidation, stolen goods and the fictional Halo trade.

Stretch wants a profitable patch with people willing to enforce it. He sees the crew as useful workers and potential competitors. Moth wants the organisation to survive a deal she suspects will discard its own members.

Bases @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.11347b4b484f139e]{CL7 Lea Bridge Social Rooms [MAPPED]} / @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b096f49f5fcfe272]{LY8 Larch Cold Store [MAPPED]}

People and division

Tessa Moth Price values territorial loyalty; collector Daz Riley wants quick money and status. Stretch favours a Meridian partnership. Moth wants an independent base. Daz and some younger adult members want escalation, while others need an exit from obligations they no longer support.

Trust and repair

Stealing from an agreed settlement or naming a protected source to an enemy makes a specific sponsor hostile. The crew can seek a faction split, restitution or a new patron rather than erase past Renown.

R18influence over membership and enforcement
R25leadership backing or a negotiated independent branch.

1 an introduction to a willing local; 2 an arranged meeting or temporary access to one faction-controlled room; 4 Moth or Stretch spends political capital to broker a major truce.

LB5 · THE LEA BOYS · MOTH

The Boy Who Kept Receipts

The Coach and Horses · Well Street Loan Office · The Red Lion · Interview Room

A junior collector kept receipts — for debts that never existed. Stretch wants the book and the boy. Moth wants the book for herself, to use against Stretch.

Objectives

  1. Meet the seller at The Coach and Horses (ticks itself)
  2. Find the duplicate books at the Well Street Loan Office (ticks itself)
  3. Make (or spring) the handover at The Red Lion (ticks itself)
  4. Decide: deliver the book, deliver both, help the seller leave, sell it twice or take it to Vale

£320 crew fee5 XP+3 Renown · The Lea Boys+1 InfluenceOffer: Renown 8

Where

@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b096f49f5fcfe272]{LY6 The Coach and Horses} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.25c01e80cc3ba50e]{WS8 Well Street Loan Office} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.f1da74521bed61fd]{SN4 The Red Lion} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.ce26d88c705b4b63]{CU4 Interview Room} MAPPED

How it plays

The job. A junior collector has records of invented debts. Stretch wants both book and collector; Moth wants an account she can use against him.

Scenes. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b096f49f5fcfe272]{LY6.3} introduces the seller at a fictional meeting. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.25c01e80cc3ba50e]{WS8.4} holds duplicate books. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.f1da74521bed61fd]{SN4.2} offers a handover or ambush; @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.ce26d88c705b4b63]{CU4} provides a different route through Vale.

Route and checks. LY / HM / CL / HC / WS / HC / CL / SN. Front for terms; Graft for the ledger; Moves for an escort or pursuit.

Pressure

The seller has a ticket out and a rival following them. After two scenes, the book moves without a deal or contested recovery.

The choice

Deliver the book, deliver both seller and book, help the seller leave, sell it twice or broker a supervised settlement.

What follows

FACTION · VC

The Velvet Circuit

Owen Pike and a council of fictional promoters. Nightlife, event bookings, contested equipment and criminal drug-market relationships.

The Circuit wants profitable nights and influence over who gets booked. Its promoters overlap with criminal suppliers, but staff, audiences and real venues are never treated as members by association. Owen sees the network as his route into property money.

Bases @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.d54307367c0dc599]{DA8 Blue Hour Basement [MAPPED]} / @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.51d4cafdaaaa0837]{ON7 North Echo Rehearsal Rooms [MAPPED]}

People and division

Door manager Reece Hale wants staff paid; performer Mara Sol wants a future without Owen's control. Owen conceals the Halo substitution and funding trail. Working promoters want independence; staff want wages and safe commitments; corporate partners want predictable content.

Trust and repair

Inventing a claim in the Circuit's name or leaving agreed wages unpaid strains the relevant promoter's support. Harm caused through criminal work produces specific victims and rivals.

R25an ownership interest, cooperative seat or independent venue agreement.

Route and checks. LY / HM / CL / HC / WS / BG / OF / VW. Graft for cargo; Savvy for the change; Front for the buyers.

Pressure

Both buyers expect the same case while a worker tries to leave. After two scenes, one buyer orders collection and the other raises the price.

The choice

Deliver the stock, arrange its withdrawal, take the rival's fee or trade its accompanying records for a more valuable concession.

What follows

The accepted brief earns its sponsor's award. Evidence supports the deliberate substitution; continuing the trade creates specific harm and opposition rather than a cost-free abstract reward.

A Set for Nobody

The Shacklewell Arms · North Echo Rehearsal Rooms · Englefield Listening Flat

There's an unreleased set out there that makes the so-called Halo warning sound like a fake. Owen wants it back. The performer who made it wants it kept safe. A collector wants it gone.

Objectives

  1. Identify the session at the backstage meeting, Shacklewell Arms (ticks itself)
  2. Get the rehearsal version at the North Echo Rehearsal Rooms (ticks itself)
  3. Find the old ident, and who reused it, at the Englefield Listening Flat
  4. Survive the contested handover at the private listening
  5. Decide: sell the rough mix, keep a copy, deliver it to Owen or bargain for a release

Scenes. VC6 · THE VELVET CIRCUIT · OWEN PIKE

The Sponsor Behind the Sponsor

The Empress · The Stratford hotel · The Baring · North Park Hospitality Lodge

Meridian wants to make Owen its official nightlife partner, and Owen wants the crew's name on the deal. What he doesn't want is anyone asking who is guaranteeing his money.

Objectives

  1. Hear the proposal over dinner at The Empress (ticks itself)
  2. Find the reception account at The Stratford hotel (ticks itself)
  3. Meet the real guarantor at The Baring (ticks itself)
  4. Give your answer at the sponsor briefing, North Park Hospitality Lodge
  5. Decide: transparent funding, sell control, take a share, expose the guarantor or build a small coalition

£480 crew fee5 XP+4 Renown · The Velvet Circuit+1 InfluenceOffer: Renown 11

Where

@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.25c01e80cc3ba50e]{WS6 The Empress} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.51d4cafdaaaa0837]{ON4 The Stratford hotel} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.357679fcd032b6ef]{HX6 The Baring} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.51d4cafdaaaa0837]{ON8 North Park Hospitality Lodge} MAPPED

Scenes. A fictional meal at @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.25c01e80cc3ba50e]{WS6.2} introduces the proposal. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.51d4cafdaaaa0837]{ON4.4} holds the reception account. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.357679fcd032b6ef]{HX6.3} brings the actual guarantor to a private meeting; @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.51d4cafdaaaa0837]{ON8.4} is the final sponsor briefing.

Pressure

The sponsor offers the crew a separate consultancy fee. Frankie needs an answer before authorising a duplicate account, and the hotel witness is leaving work.

Back transparent funding, sell control, demand a share, expose the guarantor or find a smaller independent coalition.

The accepted deal opens @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2fcc7b0410f4f526.JournalEntryPage.497596f8e42e159e]{VC7} and establishes the coordinated funding. A secret private payment remains leverage for the people who can prove it.

text.content:
VC7 · THE VELVET CIRCUIT · THE VELVET CIRCUIT

Last Dance Before the Sale

ABBA Arena · Sadler's Wells East · EartH · 3 Mills Studios

One last benefit programme could keep the circuit independent. Owen is trying to leave town with the account book before the final performance — and everyone he owes knows it.

Objectives

  1. Secure the production hire at the ABBA Arena (ticks itself)
  2. Bring in the principal act at Sadler's Wells East (ticks itself)
  3. Get the returning cases to EartH (ticks itself)
  4. Find where Owen's courier went in the rough cut at 3 Mills Studios
  5. Decide what happens to Owen and his book: witness, recovery, sale or a compromised partner

£640 crew fee5 XP+5 Renown · The Velvet Circuit+1 InfluenceOffer: Renown 15

Where

@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF1 ABBA Arena} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.7f001857f6166eed]{ST5 Sadler's Wells East} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.d54307367c0dc599]{DA5 EartH} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF4 3 Mills Studios} MAPPED

The job. A fictional benefit programme could keep the circuit independent. Owen is trying to leave with the account book before the final performance.

Scenes. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF1.4} provides an invented off-night production hire. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.7f001857f6166eed]{ST5.5} brings the principal act; @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.d54307367c0dc599]{DA5.6} supplies the returning cases. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF4.4} holds a rough cut showing where Owen's courier went.

Route and checks. BF / ST / ON / WW / HC / DA / HC / WS / BG / OF / BF. Moves or Wheels for the pursuit; Graft for recovery; Front for the show.

Pressure

A witness, unpaid act and departing van all demand attention. The programme starts after two preparation scenes; accepted allies can handle one other obligation each.

The choice

Give Owen a route to testify, recover his account by force or stealth, sell it to a rival or keep him as a compromised partner.

What follows

A delivered event funds a limited next step. A cancelled performance leaves paid contracts and rival accounts in play, and the courier remains traceable through the production crew.

Who Owns the Night

Blue Hour Basement · Marshgate Delivery Depot · London Stadium · Bridge Nine Broadcast Garage

The circuit is offering the crew a share in its future. Owen's account sits in the middle of every bargain being struck on the final night, and two promoters both want to announce the settlement.

Objectives

  1. Get the account, or its holder's terms, at the Blue Hour Basement (ticks itself)
  2. Allocate the last deliveries at the Marshgate Delivery Depot (ticks itself)
  3. Make the new ownership public at the London Stadium programme (ticks itself)
  4. Decide: a promoters' cooperative, criminal control, corporate money, a split or sell your stake

£1000 crew fee5 XP+5 Renown · The Velvet Circuit+2 InfluenceOffer: Renown 20

Where

@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.d54307367c0dc599]{DA8 Blue Hour Basement} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF7 Marshgate Delivery Depot} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.7f001857f6166eed]{ST2 London Stadium} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.7f001857f6166eed]{ST8 Bridge Nine Broadcast Garage} MAPPED

Scenes. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.d54307367c0dc599]{DA8.5} supplies the account or its holder's terms. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF7.2} allocates the last deliveries. An invented programme at @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.7f001857f6166eed]{ST2.5} and a station link through @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.7f001857f6166eed]{ST8.3} make the new ownership public.

Route and checks. DA / HC / WS / BG / OF / BF / ST. Front for ownership; Savvy for liabilities; Bottle for the final public promise.

Pressure

Two promoters claim the right to announce the settlement. Staff can withdraw from a show that hides their unpaid wages; another buyer offers immediate cash.

The choice

Form a promoters' cooperative, take criminal control, accept corporate funding, split the circuit or sell the crew's stake.

What follows

Record the actual share, venue agreements, debts and work promised. The final rank opens continuing circuit operations, with the rival promoters and affected workers shaping the next season.

FACTION · TU

The Towpath Union

Mara Tern Boyd. Couriers, transport, recovery work and contested deliveries.

The Union wants dependable routes, paid workers and the freedom to refuse a dishonest commission. Some members carry illicit goods; other drivers work ordinary jobs and choose what they accept. The crew gains influence by keeping promises when competing clients make that difficult.

Bases @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.357679fcd032b6ef]{HX7 Tern Wharf Dispatch [MAPPED]} / @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF7 Marshgate Delivery Depot [MAPPED]}

People and division

Dispatcher Gita Mercer protects workers; driver Yasmin Dale wants contracts that cannot discard her staff overnight. Tern is tempted by a funded sale. Independent drivers favour a smaller cooperative. A profitable criminal client can pull the same members in opposite directions.

Trust and repair

Selling private route contacts or abandoning a promised passenger creates a specific breach. Repairs require compensation and a new agreement from the affected worker.

What Renown earns

RankBenefit
R3reliable dispatch contact
R7priority for paid journeys
R12route-planning invitations
R18a voice in contract allocation
R25dispatch authority or a defined sale share.
Spending Influence

1 an agreed message or journey quotation; 2 a driver and vehicle booking on explicit terms; 4 coordination of a small multi-vehicle job with volunteers, fuel and capacity named.

The Wrong Case

Kingsland Courier Arch · Tern Wharf Dispatch · Hackney City Farm

A courier delivered a music case to the wrong customer. The receipt's real, but whoever signed it used somebody else's name — and the case is already being sold on.

Objectives

  1. Sort out the two deliveries at the Kingsland Courier Arch (ticks itself)
  2. Identify the substituted driver at Tern Wharf Dispatch (ticks itself)
  3. Find where the case went at the Hackney City Farm meeting (ticks itself)
  4. Decide: recover the right case, compensate the mistake, take both loads or sell it and settle with Tern

£80 crew fee3 XP+1 Renown · The Towpath Union+1 InfluenceOffer: Renown 0

Where

How it plays

The job. Tern pays the crew to recover a music case delivered to the wrong customer. The receipt is genuine but the person who signed used another name.

Scenes. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5a3e0570dd504786]{LF7.3} introduces the two deliveries. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.357679fcd032b6ef]{HX7.2} identifies the substituted driver. A fictional adult volunteer's meeting at @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b1c3f967b6aa7594]{HR5.3} reveals where the case went and why a collector wants its ordinary contents.

Pressure

A second customer is already selling the disputed case. After two enquiries, the next paid delivery removes it from the first meeting place.

The choice

Recover the right case, compensate the mistaken customer, steal both loads or accept a profitable private sale and settle with Tern.

What follows

The chosen brief opens dispatch work and access to @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5a3e0570dd504786]{LF7} and HX7. A missing case leaves a named buyer, sender and payment rather than an erased trail.

The Van and the Debt

Bow Breakers Yard · Chainring Storehouse · Barge East

TU3 · THE TOWPATH UNION · MARA "TERN" BOYD

The Driver Who Wasn't There

New Spitalfields Market administration · Orient Way railway depot · The Adam and Eve

The Glasshouse Exchange

Clement Wren. High-value theft, art and collectibles, provenance disputes and private brokerage.

The Exchange wants access to valuable objects and people who can move them. Wren can appreciate good work while knowingly profiting from a dubious title. The crew is useful when a sale needs judgement, nerve or a discreet recovery.

Bases @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.cbb65680f5cc95c5]{CG7 Glasshouse Saleroom [MAPPED]} / @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.0e780ec36ad51135]{OF5 The Trampery Fish Island Village [MAPPED]}

People and division

Restorer Luca Ferretti cares about ownership; curator Iris Bellamy wants honest loans; fixer Evie Slate prefers profitable uncertainty. Restorers want a legitimate specialist business. Criminal buyers prefer ambiguity. Wren thinks he can preserve both until a major property sale makes neutrality expensive.

Trust and repair

Falsifying an agreed appraisal or exposing unrelated clients strains access. A truthful sale to an informed buyer can still support a criminal faction's reputation.

FACTION · BB

The Backroom Bookmakers

Victor Vic Randle. Fictional betting, private lending, debt trading and criminal finance.

The Backroom wants money owed recognised and profitable deals protected. Vic likes numbers because he can pretend they remove responsibility from choices. The crew's rising status gives it access to how the accounts were created, not just how much they say someone owes.

Bases @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b096f49f5fcfe272]{LY7 Third Half Bookroom [MAPPED]} / @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.357679fcd032b6ef]{HX8 Shepherdess Coin Rooms [MAPPED]}

People and division

Cashier Eddie Lane wants genuine debts separated from invented ones; accountant Frankie Wu wants records that will survive scrutiny. Vic's redevelopment bet threatens ordinary staff. Eddie wants a fairer house. Some collectors prefer fear because it conceals the difference between an obligation and a fabrication.

Trust and repair

Secretly taking two incompatible fees or falsifying an account makes a specific creditor hostile. Correcting a record still leaves any genuine amount to negotiate.

What Renown earns

RankBenefit
R3a recognised cashier contact
R7access to the crew's own debt terms
R12finance meetings by invitation
R18a voice in major obligations
R25a defined stake or a supported alternative lending model.
Spending Influence

The job. Vic offers the crew a permanent interest as his redevelopment investment comes due. Staff and debtors bring plans that exclude him.

Scenes. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b096f49f5fcfe272]{LY7.3} compares the real liabilities. A fictional creditors' meeting at @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.a720d397aea87d6a]{HB6.3} tests a rival financing offer. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.51d4cafdaaaa0837]{ON8.4} is the final private signing, with one lender ready to walk away.

Route and checks. LY / HM / CL / SN / HB / CG / DA / HC / WW / ON. Front for ownership; Savvy for liabilities; Bottle for a binding promise.

Pressure

A neglected debtor arrives with a paid receipt while Vic demands the whole transaction remain private. One proposal can close tonight; exclusions become future claims.

The choice

Keep a predatory house, build a smaller betting business, buy Vic out, back mutual credit or sell the operation.

What follows

The final rank grants a defined financial role and actual income source. Record the original debts, collected sums, staff terms and creditors whose claims survived the deal.

FACTION · NM

The Night Market

Pearl Okonkwo. Second-hand goods, illicit resale, contested ownership and trader representation.

The Night Market is a fictional network of willing traders and brokers. It wants dependable customers and protection from people trying to own every transaction. Some members knowingly buy stolen goods; the surrounding real markets and ordinary traders are not accused by the setting.

Bases @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.0e780ec36ad51135]{OF7 Roman Exchange [MAPPED]} / @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.69084b39c04899a0]{HM2 New Spitalfields Market produce hall [MAPPED]}

People and division

Trader Nessa Grey protects her customers; broker Len Fisk wants an exclusive resale concession. Pearl favours collective bargaining. Len wants a lucrative corporate concession. Independent stallholders may choose either, or refuse to let anyone claim to represent them.

Trust and repair

Selling someone else's goods or contact details beyond the agreed terms strains the affected traders. Collective Renown depends on Pearl's mandate, not a claim that every market trader must obey her.

What Renown earns

RankBenefit
R3known broker introduction
R7priority for ordinary resale enquiries
R12access to clearance negotiations
R18a voice in network terms
R25a cooperative seat or defined concession stake.
Spending Influence

1 identifying a willing buyer or seller; 2 reserving a stall or specialist appointment at normal costs; 4 Pearl convenes a multi-party ownership settlement and commits her own standing.
